channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: itch.io Weekly New Games Roundup: Nov 2–8 (Part 2)
item.description: indienova rounds up the second half of the new games released on itch.io from Nov 2 to 8, including several indie titles built with Godot — worth a browse for developers looking for inspiration or gameplay references.

item.title: Unreal Engine 5.4 ArchViz Optimization: Slashing Draw Calls from 10,000 to Under 1,200
item.description: Architectural models imported from Revit and similar tools can easily hit 10,000 draw calls, so the author batches repeated elements with hierarchical instanced static meshes and holds large scenes at a steady 60 FPS.

item.title: Building NICHLYST: The Gate That Stayed Open — 33 Endings, 32 Green Tests, One Honest Caveat
item.description: After fixing 704 failing assertions, the author validates 33 endings and bilingual fields with a run of small, narrow checks — then admits the phase gates passed while a known device-side startup error still awaits a real device run, so green tests prove only what they prove.

item.title: Clannect Engine v0.2 Is Here: A Major Step Towards Open Release
item.description: Clannect Engine has reached v0.2, another key step toward its open release, and developers tracking small engines should keep an eye on its progress.

item.title: A Blackjack Table That Lives in a README, Dealt by GitHub Actions
item.description: A playable blackjack table that lives in a README: place a bet via an issue, a workflow reads it, and the README redraws the hand.

item.title: Why "Optimized" GIFs Turn Into Haunted Sprite Sheets (And 4 Tiny Canvas Fixes for 2D Game Devs)
item.description: Feeding 'optimized' GIFs into a custom importer often misaligns sprite sheets, and this article breaks down the cause and offers four small Canvas fixes.

item.title: Checking a Four-Direction Sprite Sheet Before Importing It
item.description: Quickly check a four-direction walk cycle's frame count and facing before import, so characters do not walk wrong in-game.

item.title: Throwing Out the Widget Tree: Building a 2D Game Engine Underneath Flutter (Sting)
item.description: The author shares building the 2D game engine Sting from scratch under Flutter, focusing on large-scale unit simulation on hex grids.

item.title: Engineering 60FPS Multiplayer Browser Games with HTML5 Canvas & WebSockets (Ludo, Stickman & Clicker)
item.description: The author breaks down how zero-install browser multiplayer games use client prediction and deterministic state machines to lock 60fps, a useful reference for indies wanting lightweight web multiplayer.

item.title: The Invisible Brush: Generative Art and the Algorithms That Paint
item.description: A hands-on tour of procedural content generation as a creative craft in Clojure and Quil, from seeds to terrain and galaxies, ending with a working piece of generative art.

item.title: 41 browser games, one canvas codebase: how we ship them to a dozen portals
item.description: A small team built 41 HTML5 games on a plain JavaScript canvas with no engine, shipping them to a dozen portals through the Playgama Bridge SDK and sharing the real costs and trade-offs of multi-portal distribution.

item.title: Designing a Gamified Fitness Loop: Translating Raw Pedometer Streams into Virtual Companion State
item.description: This dev diary explains how raw pedometer streams from OS health APIs are layered into a state engine that drives a virtual companion without feeling broken or exploitable.

item.title: In-App Purchase Implementation Guide for Mobile Games
item.description: A practical walkthrough of the full mobile in-app purchase flow — fetching products, starting purchases, validating transactions server-side, then granting items — to help indie developers avoid common IAP pitfalls.

item.title: Humble Fumbles & November GameDev Deals Round-Up
item.description: A round-up of November deals and bundles for game developers, including the Unity Asset Store low-poly mega bundle — a good moment to stock up on tools and art assets at a discount.

item.title: What's inside an .osk file? Packaging an osu! skin correctly
item.description: A clear breakdown of what's inside an .osk file and how to package an osu! skin correctly, whether you're building skin tools or sharing an edited skin with a friend.

item.title: Building a Custom HTML5 Canvas + Synced Video Engine for Real-Time Combat Dialogue (V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura)
item.description: This Brazilian indie action-adventure skips Unity, Unreal and Godot for a custom HTML5 Canvas engine layered over synced MP4 scenes, with real-time companion dialogue and multilingual voice switching in combat.

item.title: Dedicated server or VDS? A practical way to decide for databases, game servers and CI
item.description: Starting from real symptoms like CPU wobble and latency spikes, this guide helps you decide whether your game server needs a dedicated box or a VDS with pinned cores.

item.title: Build 60 FPS Particle Explosions in 10 Lines of Vanilla JS with AI Prompts
item.description: This tutorial shows how to use HTML5 Canvas and an AI prompting workflow to build buttery 60 FPS particle bursts in just 10 lines of code.

item.title: I built 10 tiny Windows tools for the boring parts of indie gamedev
item.description: One small tool per recurring jam chore — batch-resizing sprites, slicing tilesheets, packing atlases, generating retro sound effects — bundled as a toolkit indie devs can use to save hours.

item.title: Blind Sight: Dead World Demo on Android: Design Lessons From a Tiny Zombie Survival Game
item.description: A first-person zombie survival demo built on just three mechanics — scavenge, defend, escape — and the author breaks down how scarce resources force meaningful choices, a useful lesson for small teams building demos.
